# Which scenarios to record, for every kind of instrument

<!-- Generated by tools/make_scenarios.py from chromiq_probe/sessions/*.json. -->

One sitting with the right set of recordings answers more than many small rounds. For each kind of instrument there is one ordered list of short blocks, the most useful first within a sensible order for one sitting. Each block says what to do in the maker's own program, one action per line, what to note, and why we need it. The tool's guided session walks you through exactly the same list (the tool and these pages are made from the same files), shows how far you are, and writes into the zip which blocks were recorded and which were skipped.

| Kind of instrument | Blocks | Essential | All, about | Short set, about | Built on |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Handheld spot and strip instrument](docs/scenarios/handheld.md) | 21 | 10 | 56 min | 20 min | real recordings |
| [Motorised table (xy)](docs/scenarios/table.md) | 23 | 13 | 97 min | 20 min | real recordings |
| [Sheet-fed chart reader](docs/scenarios/sheetfed.md) | 13 | 8 | 40 min | 20 min | our reasoning |
| [Network-connected instrument](docs/scenarios/network.md) | 14 | 8 | 43 min | 20 min | our reasoning |
| [Serial instrument (RS-232)](docs/scenarios/serial.md) | 14 | 9 | 38 min | 20 min | our reasoning |
| [Something else](docs/scenarios/other.md) | 12 | 7 | 40 min | 18 min | our reasoning |

Priorities: **essential** (without these a recording answers little), **important** (each answers a question we have needed before), **nice to have**. The **short set** is a 20-minute choice from the essential blocks, with at least one untidy ending.

**The maker's manual wins.** If anything here contradicts what the maker's manual says about handling your instrument, follow the manual and skip the block. Nothing in these lists asks you to force a moving part by hand.

Display colorimeters (the small pucks for screens) are not covered: ArgyllCMS already supports most of them, and their steps are different.

An example of the same plan for one model: [X-Rite i1iO 3](docs/scenarios/example-xrite-i1io3.md).

To write a session file for one particular instrument, see [SESSIONS.md](SESSIONS.md).
